name: ❌ ♡ Low FODMAP Gazpacho
ingredients:
25 gr gluten-free white bread (I used the no crust white bread by Proceli, which is sold in several European countries)
187 1/2 gr tomatoes*
88 g smoked red bell pepper*  🔴 Fructose 205%
1/4 cucumber
1.4 ml (garlic) olive oil ♥ Sat fat 0.2g (1%)
1/2 tbsp wine vinegar
Salt
directions:
1. Soak the white bread in cold water for 2 minutes. The gluten-free bread that I used was very soft already. If you use another kind of bread you might have to soak it a bit longer, 10-15 minutes. Squeeze the water out of the bread and tear it into pieces.

2. Cut the tomato, cucumber and bell pepper into cubes.

3. If you don’t have low FODMAP olive oil, you can make it yourself by heating olive oil in a pan and then adding one or two cloves of garlic. Heat the garlic in the oil for a while and then remove it. Leave the oil to cool down.

4. Put the tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, bread and olive oil into a bowl. Put everything into a blender and blend into a smooth mixture. Flavour with salt and vinegar.

5. Put the gazpacho mixture through a sieve and put it into the fridge for several hours to cool.

6. Serve the soup with a garnish of your choice. For example some pieces of cucumber and bell pepper, parsley, spring onion or olives in pieces.
description:
A delicious Spanish low FODMAP gazpacho. Traditional cold soup made with tomatoes, bell pepper, cucumber and gluten-free white bread. A perfect summer soup!

🔴 Fructose 205%

♡ Sat fat 0.2g (1%)
notes: Imported for personal use. Check Monash app for current serve sizes.

name: ❌ ♡ Low FODMAP salmorejo
ingredients:
1 kg vine tomatoes*  🔴 Fructose 385%
200 g white bread (I use Schär Meisterbäckers classic)
50 ml olive oil ♥ Sat fat 1.7g (8%)
1 tbsp red wine vinegar
1/2 tsp salt
1/2 tsp pepper
2 hardboiled eggs** ♥ Sat fat 0.8g (4%)
60 g serranoham or bacon, cut into cubes** ♥ Sat fat 1.8g (9%)
directions:
1. Boil two eggs hard (8 to 10 min). Drain and set aside to cool down.

2. Cut an X into the bottom of each tomato. Put the tomatoes into a pan with boiling water for 30 seconds.

3. Drain and leave the tomatoes to cool down. Then you can easily remove the skin.

4. Cut the tomatoes into cubes. Put them into a bowl and use an (immersion) blender to turn them into a puree.

5. Tear the bread into small pieces and add to the bowl. Add the olive oil, red wine vinegar, pepper and salt. Blend into a smooth soup.

6. Taste the soup and add extra pepper, salt and olive oil to taste.

7. The soup tastes best when it is cooled. So put it into the fridge for at least one hour before you serve the soup.

8. Cut the Serrano ham into cubes and cut the eggs into pieces.

9. Divide the soup over four bowls and garnish each bowl with half of a boiled egg and some Serrano ham.
description:
A delicious Spanish dish: low FODMAP salmorejo! A yummy cold starter. Simple and easy to make. Gluten-free and lactose-free. With vega and vegan option.

♡ Sat fat 4.3g (21%)

name: ❌ ♡ Low FODMAP Vodka Pasta Sauce
ingredients:
1 pound carrots (about 3 large, unpeeled and cut into 1-inch chunks)
1.5 pound vine tomatoes  🔴 Fructose 262%
1/2 fennel bulb
Olive oil
Sea salt
1 cup vegetable stock or water
12 ounces gluten-free penne  🟠 Fructans 57%
1/3 cup basil leaves
Red pepper flakes
directions:
1. Preheat your oven to 230°C. Line a sheet pan with parchment paper.

2. Arrange the tomatoes, carrots and fennel on the sheet pan and season with 1 teaspoon sea salt. Drizzle the vegetables generously with olive oil, arrange in an even layer cut-side down so each piece touches the pan, and transfer to the oven.

3. Roast until the tomatoes are shriveled and have released their juices and the carrots are tender, about 40 minutes. Remove the pan from the oven.

4. Transfer the vegetables to a high-powered blender, along with the vegetable stock or water, and puree until smooth, adding more broth as necessary. Store the sauce for later in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 weeks, or proceed and make pasta.

5. To make pasta: bring a large pot of salted water to boil. Cook the pasta according to package directions. Reserve 1 cup of starchy pasta water, then drain in a colander. Return the pasta to the pan along with 1 cup vodka sauce, adding some of the pasta water to loosen it up if it seems too thick. Add more sauce as necessary and save the remainder for another use.

6. Divide the penne alla vodka between bowls and garnish with basil, red pepper flakes and a dash of olive oil, if using.
description:
This lightened up version of vodka sauce uses roasted carrots, tomatoes and fennel to create a super flavorful, creamy sauce without any added cream or thickener. It’s a low FODMAP tomato sauce that is also gluten-free, dairy-free and packed with nutrients. Simply toss it together with your favorite gluten-free penne pasta!

name: ❌ 💔 Chocolate Chip Banana Bread Pudding (Gluten and Dairy-Free)
ingredients:
100 g can full-fat coconut milk  🔴 Sorbitol 167% 💔 Sat fat 19g (95%)
3/4 large eggs ((see note)) ♥ Sat fat 1.2g (6%)
1/2 tbsp maple syrup
1/2 tbsp coconut oil or ghee ( melted, plus more for greasing) 💔 Sat fat 6.2g (31%)
1/4 very ripe banana (roughly mashed)
1/4 tsp vanilla extract
1/8 tsp sea salt
1/8 loaf gluten-free sandwich bread
1/8 cup walnuts or pecans (chopped)
1/8 cup dark chocolate chunks 💔 Sat fat 5.4g (27%)
directions:
1. Make the dairy-free custard: in a large bowl, whisk together the coconut milk, eggs, maple syrup, coconut oil or ghee, banana, vanilla, and sea salt until smooth.

2. Grease a 9x13 casserole dish with coconut oil or ghee. Roughly tear apart the gluten-free bread into 2-inch pieces and arrange in the pan in an even-ish layer (you should have around 4 cups total. Top with the walnuts or pecans, and chocolate.

3. Pour the non dairy custard over the bread, using your hands or a spatula to press down any rogue pieces so they are all more or less submerged. Allow the bread to rest at room temperature for at least an hour so it absorbs the custard, or cover and place in the fridge to sit overnight.

4. When ready to bake the banana bread pudding, preheat the oven to 205°C.

5. Transfer the banana bread pudding casserole dish to the middle of the oven and bake for about 40 minutes, or until puffed and lightly browned on top.

6. Remove the banana bread pudding from the oven and allow it to rest in the pan for at least 10 minutes before cutting into it. Then serve topped with dairy-free vanilla ice cream or crème fraiche, if needed.
description:
This banana bread pudding gets a lighter spin thanks to a dairy-free custard with coconut milk and gluten-free bread. Which just means more room for chocolate chips!

💔 Sat fat 109.8g (549%)

name: ❌ 💔 18+ Low FODMAP desserts: Coconut Lime Paletas (Ice Pops)
ingredients:
1/4 cup maple syrup
1/4 cup water (or pure cane sugar)
400 g can full fat coconut milk  🔴 Sorbitol 667%  💔 Sat fat 76g (380%)
1/2 cup freshly squeezed lime juice (about 4-6 juicy limes)
1/4 cup lightly packed coriander (leaves and tender stems)
1/4 cup prepared simple syrup
2 tbsp pure cane sugar
1/2 tsp lime zest ((zest of 1 medium lime))
directions:
1. Place the maple syrup and water in a small pot. Over medium heat, bring the mixture to a simmer and stir until syrup is dissolved, about 2-3 minutes. Remove the mixture from the heat and cool to room temperature.

2. You can make your pops in layers of coconut and lime or you can just blend the whole thing together for ease! To make blended popsicles, simply add coconut milk, lime juice, coriander, simple syrup, sugar and lime zest to a blender and blend until smooth, about 1 minute. Pour into popsicle molds and freeze for at least 4 hours or overnight.

3. To make layered popsicles: In a blender, blend coconut milk and sugar until combined. Pour into a liquid measuring cup, stir in the lime zest and set aside.

4. Rinse the blender and add the lime juice, coriander and ¼ cup of the cooled simple syrup. Blend until smooth, about a minute. Taste and add more simple syrup if you like your popsicles sweeter.

5. To assemble the popsicles: start with the coconut milk mixture and fill molds 1/3 full. Freeze for about an hour, or until lightly set. Add a layer of the coriander lime mixture and freeze again for about an hour. Finally add the remaining layer of the coconut milk mixture. Using a wooden skewer or chopstick, swirl the layers together if you wish. Freeze for 4 hours or overnight.
description:
This sweet-tart treat is perfect for a summer day! Coconut, lime and coriander (yes, coriander!) make for a grown up treat that you will love. Vegan, gluten free and low FODMAP when you stick to a 1 pop serving.

🔴 Sorbitol 667%

💔 Sat fat 76g (380%)
notes: Imported for personal use. Check Monash app for current serve sizes.

name: ❌ 💔 Gluten-free quiche caprese
ingredients:
120 ml cold water
1 tbsp apple cider vinegar  🟢 Fructose 19% (3.8 g per serving)
150 g gluten-free flour (I used Schär Mix It Universal) or a mix of gluten-free flour mix and buckwheat flour  🟢 Fructans 38% (38 g per serving)
1/2 tsp xanthan gum
A pinch of salt
100 g cold butter, in cubes  💔 Sat fat 12.8g (64%)
A 22 cm (8.75 inch) quiche pan
1 tbsp gluten-free breadcrumbs
5 eggs  ♥ Sat fat 2g (10%)
300 gram cherry tomatoes, halved or roma tomatos, sliced*  🔴 Fructose 167% (75 g per serving)
1 green or red bell pepper*  🟠 Fructose 93% (40 g per serving)
250 ml lactose-free whipped cream  💔 Sat fat 12.5g (62%)
1 handful of fresh basil
1/2 tsp pepper
1/2 tsp salt
1 buffalo mozzarella
A handful of fresh basil
directions:
For the crust
1. Mix the cold water with the apple cider vinegar and put this into the freezer until you need it.

2. Sieve the gluten-free flour with the xanthan gum and the salt in a bowl.

3. Add the cubes of butter and knead this with your fingers until you have fine crumbles.

4. Add the cold water-vinegar mixture. Add a tablespoon at a time and mix the dough with a for until it starts to stick together. You need about 6-8 tablespoons.

5. Form the dough into a disk and wrap it in cling film and leave to rest in the fridge for at least 1 hour.

6. Pre-heat the oven to 200°C.

7. Roll out the dough until it is about 2-3 mm thin and larger than the pie tin in diameter, about 28-30 cm (11-12 inches).

8. Carefully lift up the pie crust and lay it over the baking tin. Carefully press it into the tin. Remove any pastry that is sticking over the edge.

9. Refrigerate the crust for another 15 minutes.

10. Prick the bottom of the crust with a fork and bake for 10 minutes.

11. Lower the oven temperature to 180°C.

12. Divide 1 tbsp gluten-free breadcrumbs over the quiche crust.

For the filling
13. Beat the eggs with the lactose-free cream in a bowl. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.

14. Wash the cherry tomatoes and cut them in half. Spread the cherry tomatoes over the bottom of the quiche.

15. Wash the bell pepper and cut into small pieces. Spread this over the quiche base as well.

16. Pour the egg mixture into the quiche tin.

17. Spread the fresh basil over it.

18. Cut the mozzarella into slices and divide it over the quiche.

19. Place the quiche in the oven for 45 minutes.
description:
A vegetarian quiche inspired on caprese salad: gluten-free quiche caprese! With mozzarella, tomato and basil. Low FODMAP and low lactose.

💔 Sat fat 27.2g (136%)

directions:

ingredients:

directions:

name: ℹ️ ❣ Warm & Creamy Spinach Dip (Dairy + Gluten-Free)

30 ml 1 cup plant-based sour cream  🟠 Lactose 75% 💔 Sat fat 6g (30%)

1/8 mayonnaise or vegan alternative
1/8 tsp sea salt
1/8 crushed red pepper flakes or chili crisp  🟡 Fructose 47%
1/8 gluten-free breadcrumbs or panko
32 oz frozen spinach (2 packages, thawed see note)
0.03 cup grated Parmesan cheese (optional) ♥ Sat fat 1.2g (6%)
directions:
1. Preheat the oven to 175°C.

2. Gather the spinach in a clean dish towel and squeeze out all the moisture over the sink. You should have two golf balls of spinach. Set aside in a medium mixing bowl.

3. To the spinach, add the dairy-free cream cheese, sour cream, mayonnaise,

4. red pepper flakes, salt. Stir until all the ingredients are fully incorporated. Pour the mixture into a small (6-inch) cast-iron skillet or ovenproof baking dish.

description:
This oven-baked gluten-free spinach dip is impossibly creamy and satisfying, despite being made with dairy-free cream cheese and sour cream. It makes enough to feed a crowd, but can also be scaled down for more intimate gatherings – just halve the recipe. If you're not dairy-free, a little fresh grated Parmesan on top is a lovely accompaniment to the gluten-free breadcrumbs. Simply omit the garlic for a low FODMAP dip. To make this dairy-free spinach dip vegan too, omit the parmesan and use plant-based mayonnaise. My preferred brand for the cream cheese and sour cream is this one. If your frozen spinach is not pre-thawed, it’s easy to nuke it in a microwave safe bowl until soft, then follow the recipe to remove the moisture. If you can only find 10-ounce boxes of frozen spinach, it’s totally fine to go with 30 ounces (3 packages) versus the 32 ounces total called for in the recipe.

name: ℹ️ ♡ Low FODMAP shrimp lo mein noodles
ingredients:
70 g soba noodles*  🟡 Fructans 47%
100 g shrimps
66 g oyster mushrooms
1/2 small romaine lettuce or 150 g bok choy
1 stalks of spring onion, the green part.  🟢 Fructose 16%
50 g carrots
1/4 green bell pepper  🟠 Fructans 53%
3/4 tbsp cornstarch
2 tbsp soy sauce*
1/2 tbsp mirin
1/2 sesame oil
1/2 black pepper
directions:
**Prep (bowls):**

**Large bowl — noodles (boil later):**
- Have the soba noodles ready to cook.

**Large bowl — shrimp (fry last):**
- Have the shrimps ready; thaw if frozen. Pat dry.

**Large bowl — mushrooms (fry):**
- Clean the oyster mushrooms and cut into pieces.

**Large bowl — veg (fry / soften):**
- Wash the lettuce or bok choy; trim ends and cut into pieces (keep firmer white parts separate from green if using lettuce).
- Slice the spring onion greens into rings.
- Cut the carrots and green bell pepper into small pieces.

**Small bowl — slurry (thicken sauce):**
- Mix the cornstarch with a little water to a thick slurry.

By the hob (no bowl): soy sauce, mirin, sesame oil, black pepper, oil for the wok.

**1. Sauce:** Stir together soy sauce, mirin, sesame oil, and black pepper. Whisk in the slurry. Keep by the hob.

**2. Noodles:** Boil the noodles bowl per packet; drain, rinse with cold water, and set aside.

**3. Stir-fry veg:** Heat oil in a wok on high. Fry carrots, bell pepper, mushrooms, and the firmer lettuce/bok choy stems briefly. Add the leafy greens and spring onion; fry another minute.

**4. Sauce & shrimp:** Pour in the sauce and heat briefly. Add the shrimp bowl and fry until pink.

**5. Finish:** Add the noodles and toss. Serve immediately.

name: ✅ ❣ Low FODMAP meatballs in tomato sauce
ingredients:
500 g minced meat (50% pork, 50% beef)
1 egg ♥ Sat fat 1.6g (8%)
1 tbsp oat flour or gluten-free breadcrumbs  🟢 Fructans 4%
1 tbsp mustard (choose a low FODMAP version)
1 tsp cumin (for the meatballs)
1 tsp smoked paprika
1 cayenne pepper
Pepper and salt
2 stalks of spring onion, the green part only  🟡 Fructose 32%
½ tsp cumin (for the tomato sauce)
1 tsp chilli powder
½ tsp oregano
A pinch of salt
2 tbsp gluten-free flour  🟢 Fructans 16%
2 tbsp olive oil ❣ Sat fat 3.8g (19%)
500 ml stock (make sure to pick a low FODMAP version)
1 can of pureed tomato
directions:
**Prep (bowls):**

**Large bowl — meatballs (poach):**
- Have the minced meat ready.
- Slice the spring onion greens.
- Have mustard, oat flour or breadcrumbs, cumin, smoked paprika, cayenne, pepper and salt ready beside this bowl.
- Have the egg ready.

**Small bowl — sauce spice mix (fry):**
- Mix the chilli powder, cumin, oregano and a pinch of salt.
- Have the gluten-free flour ready beside this bowl.

By the hob (no bowl): olive oil, stock (sauce and poaching), pureed tomato.

**1. Sauce:** Heat olive oil; stir in flour, then the sauce spice mix bowl until fragrant. Whisk in stock and pureed tomato. Boil, then simmer about 15 minutes.

**2. Meatballs:** Mix meat with egg, mustard, oat flour or breadcrumbs, meat spices and spring onion; knead and roll into balls.

**3. Poach:** Bring stock to the boil; poach the meatballs about 5 minutes. Drain; add to the tomato sauce. Serve now or cool and reheat before serving.

name: ✅ ♡ Soup - Tom Yum Soup
ingredients:
113 g raw shrimp, peeled and deveined, shells reserved for stock
1/2 stalks lemongrass, tough outer layer removed, bruised and cut into 2-inch lengths
1/4 thumb-size piece galangal, or fresh ginger as a swap
1 3/8 kaffir lime leaves, lightly torn
5/8 fresh red bird's eye chilies, sliced
34 g oyster mushrooms, torn into bite-size strips
2 cherry tomatoes, halved
2 spring onion green tops, thinly sliced  🟢 Fructose 32%
1/4 coriander leaves, roughly torn
1/2 tbsp olive oil  ♥ Sat fat 0.9g (5%)
1 1/2 cup low-FODMAP chicken broth, or homemade shrimp stock from the reserved shells
3/4 tbsp fish sauce
7/8 tbsp fresh lime juice (about 2 limes)
1/4 tsp cane sugar or maple syrup
1 canned coconut milk, for a creamy version (optional, up to; see Tips)
Optional: up to 1/4 cup (60 ml) canned coconut milk for a creamy version (see Tips)
directions:
**Prep (bowls):**

**Large bowl — shrimp (poach later):**
- Peel and devein the shrimp; reserve shells if making shrimp stock.

**Small bowl — aromatics (fry / infuse):**
- Bruise and cut the lemongrass.
- Slice the galangal or ginger.
- Lightly tear the kaffir lime leaves.
- Slice the bird's eye chilies (reserve some for serving).

**Medium bowl — mushrooms & tomato (simmer later):**
- Tear the oyster mushrooms into strips.
- Halve the cherry tomatoes.

**Medium bowl — finish:**
- Thinly slice the spring onion greens.
- Roughly tear the coriander.
- Have the reserved chili ready.

By the hob (no bowl): olive oil, chicken broth (or water for shell stock), fish sauce, lime juice, sugar or maple syrup, optional coconut milk.

**1. Broth:** If using shells, simmer them in the broth or water about 10 minutes, then strain. Otherwise start with the chicken broth.

**2. aromatics bowl:** Warm olive oil over medium heat. Stir the aromatics bowl (use half the chili) about 1 minute until fragrant. Pour in the broth; simmer uncovered 12–15 minutes to infuse.

**3. Mushrooms:** Add the mushrooms & tomato bowl; simmer 3–4 minutes until the mushrooms soften.

**4. Shrimp:** Add the shrimp bowl; cook 2–3 minutes until pink and opaque (do not boil hard).

**5. Season:** Off the heat, stir in fish sauce, lime juice and sugar. Taste and balance salty, sour and sweet. Optional: stir in coconut milk for a creamier version.

**6. Serve:** Ladle into bowls (leave lemongrass and galangal behind if preferred). Top with the finish bowl.

Cool, portion, refrigerate up to 3 days; reheat gently until piping hot (do not overcook the shrimp).
description:
A low FODMAP tom yum of shrimp, oyster mushrooms, lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, bird's eye chilies, fish sauce, lime, and cherry tomatoes. Gluten-free and dairy-free.

🟢 Fructose 32%

♡ Sat fat 0.9g (5%)

name: ❌ 💔 Low FODMAP Coconut Chia Pudding with Cantaloupe
ingredients:
⅓ cup canned coconut milk  🔴 Sorbitol 133%  💔 Sat fat 15.2g (76%)
¼ cup water
2 tablespoons chia seeds
1 teaspoon maple syrup
¼ cup diced cantaloupe
200 g blueberries  🔴 Fructose 160%
directions:
1. In a small bowl, whisk together coconut milk, water, chia seeds, and maple syrup until well mixed.

2. Cover and refrigerate until a gel-like mixture has formed, at least 2 hours. I recommend stirring the mixture after about an hour in the fridge to redistribute the chia seeds as they tend to settle to the bottom.

3. Serve pudding chilled and topped with diced cantaloupe, blueberries, and optional mint leaves.

name: ❌ ♡ Smoothie - Green Smoothie
ingredients:
1.5 cups fresh baby spinach, loosely packed
1 small firm-yellow banana, still slightly green at the tips  🔴 Fructans 126%
1 cup fresh or frozen pineapple chunks  🔴 Fructans 171%
1/8 cup low FODMAP milk (unsweetened almond, soy-protein soy or lactose-free semi-skimmed)  ♥ Sat fat 0.3g (2%)
1/2 cup ice (skip if the pineapple is frozen)
1 teaspoon pure maple syrup
1/2 teaspoon fresh lime juice
directions:
Blend
1. Add the milk to the blender first, then the spinach. Blend on high for 20 seconds to break down the leaves before any fruit goes in.

2. Add the banana, pineapple, ice, maple, and lime. Blend on high for 30 to 60 seconds, until smooth and uniformly green.

3. Pour into a glass and drink right away. The texture thins and the color darkens as it sits.
